jim_customer: Hey team — we flipped on batching for our embeddings pipeline ~30m ago and now batched requests (size 4-8) intermittently return a 500 with 'dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 768'. Single-item calls still succeed. Trace id: t-8f3a9c2. Any idea?

priya_support: sorry you're hitting this, can you paste a minimal repro (cURL or SDK snippet) and confirm which model you're calling and the embedding dimension you expect? Also are you mixing raw strings + vectors in the same batch? :thinking_face:

jim_customer: model=text-embed-1536, expecting 1536 dims. We're calling via the JS SDK v1.4.1, payload is an array of strings (not vectors). Example: 
```
await client.embeddings.create({
  model: 'text-embed-1536',
  input: ["line one", "line two", "line three"]
})
```
We didn't intentionally send vectors.

priya_support: thanks. can you share one failing request id from the trace or the full request/response log (redact user data)? helps us match to routing logs.

jim_customer: here's the trace from our side: trace=t-8f3a9c2, request_id=R-44321. Response body (sanitized): 500 {"error":"dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 768"}. Occurs ~30% of batches, no obvious pattern.

eli_infra: tagging in infra. priya, i've pulled the routing logs for R-44321. Seen something interesting: the batch was dynamically split across two model backends — one backend was text-embed-1536 (expected 1536), the other was text-embed-768 (legacy / quant variant). One of the batch items was flagged as 'pre-embedded' by the SDK (content type detection) and treated differently during batching. attaching excerpt: 
```
ROUTE: batch_id=B-997, shards=[srv-a:text-embed-1536, srv-z:text-embed-768]
ITEMS: [item0:type=string, item1:type=vector(len=768), item2:type=string]
```

priya_support: whoa — that would explain it. jim, do you ever pass precomputed vectors to the same endpoint (some parts of pipeline send vectors, others send raw text)?

jim_customer: ah — yes, we have a legacy path that sometimes enriches input with precomputed embeddings (search feature). But we thought we filtered those out before the batch call. Looks like a bug in our batching collector — it accidentally pushed precomputed vectors into the same input array for some request windows.

maria_ml: quick note — the embeddings endpoint accepts both strings and numeric arrays, but the server expects homogenous inputs per batch. Dynamic batching can combine multiple requests, but if items inside the aggregated batch are mixed (strings + vectors) and those vectors have differing dims, routing can end up sending subsets to different model variants and surface a dimension mismatch. So the root cause is mixed input types (or precomputed vectors with a different dim).

sam_sdk: SDK note — older clients (<=1.4.1) do a lightweight content sniff to guess input type; they may not always mark items explicitly. We just released 1.4.3 that adds an explicit per-item content_type header and validates homogeneity before sending. Upgrading should help prevent accidental mixing.

priya_support: immediate mitigation options: 1) ensure you send only strings (or only vectors) per embeddings.create call; 2) split problematic batches server-side so precomputed vectors never get mixed; 3) set max_batch_size=1 or reduce batching window to avoid multi-request aggregation while you patch the collector. For Dedicated customers we can also toggle dynamic_batching:false for your deployment — ping if you want us to do that temporarily.

jim_customer: thanks — we rolled a fix to the collector (filtering out vectors) and are going to upgrade the SDK. For the short-term I'll set max_batch_size=1. What's the config knob for that?

nina_prodops: if you're on Hosted API you can control client-side options. For Dedicated we expose a config under inference.runtime.batch.max_batch_size. Example in Dedicated YAML: 
```
inference:
  runtime:
    batch:
      max_batch_size: 1
      batching_window_ms: 25
```
If you need us to apply it, tell me the tenant id and I can apply a temporary override.

jim_customer: tenant=cust-984. Please apply override for the next 1 hour while we finish SDK rollout.

nina_prodops: done — applied override and restarted the pool. ops_bot:deploy_status shows healthy.

ops_bot: Deployment update: batch-config-override applied to cust-984; pool restart completed at 2026-03-15T14:12:08Z.

eli_infra: digging deeper — we saw ~18 affected batches in the last 40m. All had one or more items where client payload arrived as a JSON array of numbers (len 768). Those were from your other service that enriches search. After we blocked batching across mixed types the backend no longer tried to route to mixed model variants.

priya_support: follow-ups for triage: - jim, confirm SDK upgrade to >=1.4.3 and that collector filter is active. - sam, can we add a server-side guard to reject mixed-type batches with a 400 and clearer error message (instead of 500 dimension mismatch)? That would make this class of bug easier for customers to act on.

sam_sdk: good idea. I'll open a GH issue and PR for the SDK and raise an infra ticket to add a prebatch validation that returns 400 {"error":"mixed_input_types_in_batch"}.

jim_customer: confirmed — collector fix deployed, SDK upgrade started (canary at 10%). I set client-side max_batch_size=1 for now, errors have stopped. Please keep the override for 1 hour then revert. Thanks all. :pray:

priya_support: great to hear — marking this thread with root cause: mixed input types (strings + precomputed vectors of different dims) causing dynamic batching to route to incompatible model variants which surfaced a dimension mismatch 500. Action items recorded: 1) customer deploys collector fix + SDK upgrade; 2) prodops temporary override applied; 3) infra to add validation and better error (sam to own). Closing once override reverted and canary passes.

nina_prodops: will revert override at 15:30 UTC unless you ask to extend.

jim_customer: can you leave it for the hour, we'll message if we need more time. Thanks again! :thumbsup:
